title: Quiet holidays abroad: relaxing places to properly slow down
author: Matt
intro: If your idea of a perfect holiday is a book, a swim and nowhere to be, here are the quiet, relaxing places worth the trip, near and far, plus when to go so they stay peaceful.
seo_title: Quiet holidays abroad: relaxing places to slow down
seo_description: The best quiet and relaxing holiday destinations abroad, from Gozo, Menorca and the Azores to Mauritius and Luang Prabang, with when to go to avoid the crowds and tips for a peaceful trip.

sections.heading: The short list
sections.text:
- **Short flight, island calm:** [Gozo](/destinations/gozo), [Menorca](/destinations/menorca) and [Madeira](/destinations/madeira).
- **Nature and space:** the [Azores](/destinations/azores) and [Lake Garda](/destinations/lake-garda) in spring or autumn.
- **Slow old towns:** [Syracuse](/destinations/syracuse) in Sicily and [Matera](/destinations/matera) in southern Italy.
- **Far away, worth it:** [Mauritius](/destinations/mauritius), [the Maldives](/destinations/maldives), [Luang Prabang](/destinations/luang-prabang) and the [Bacalar](/destinations/bacalar) lagoon in Mexico.

For more, see all our [relaxing holidays](/destinations/relaxing-holidays), with the best months for each.

sections.heading: What makes a holiday quiet
sections.text: It's less about the place than about when you go and where you stay. Even busy islands have calm corners, and even quiet towns fill up in August. The places below are naturally slow-paced, small or spread out, so they stay peaceful for most of the year, and we've said when they're at their quietest.

sections.heading: Near: a short flight away
sections.text:
[Gozo](/destinations/gozo) is Malta's smaller, greener sister island, a short ferry ride from Malta. It's all quiet bays, salt pans, farmhouses with pools and some of the clearest water in the Mediterranean. It feels a world away from the busier main island.

[Menorca](/destinations/menorca) is the calm one of the Balearics, a UNESCO biosphere reserve with pine-backed coves and small harbour towns. The south coast has the sandy beaches; the north is wilder. June and September are lovely and much quieter than August.

[Madeira](/destinations/madeira) is about four hours from the UK and mild all year, with garden hotels, levada walks along the mountainsides and pools rather than beaches. It's one of the best places in Europe for a peaceful winter break.

sections.heading: Nature, space and fresh air
sections.text:
The [Azores](/destinations/azores) are nine volcanic islands in the middle of the Atlantic, about four hours from London. There are crater lakes, hot springs, whale watching and green hills full of cows, and no big resorts. It's never hot, which suits people who'd rather walk than lie by a pool.

[Lake Garda](/destinations/lake-garda) gets very busy in July and August, but in May, June and September it's at its best: warm days, ferries between quiet towns and lakeside lunches. The north of the lake is calmer than the busy resorts in the south.

sections.heading: Slow old towns
sections.text:
[Syracuse](/destinations/syracuse) in Sicily mixes Greek ruins, swimming from the rocks in Ortigia and long, lazy lunches. In May, June, September and October it's warm, calm and easy-going.

[Matera](/destinations/matera) is a town of cave houses carved into a gorge, and staying in a cave hotel is one of the most peaceful experiences in Italy, especially in the evening, when the day-trippers leave and the lights come on.

sections.heading: Far away, and worth the flight
sections.text:
[Mauritius](/destinations/mauritius) and [the Maldives](/destinations/maldives) are the classic choices for a relaxing beach holiday: calm lagoons, resorts made for doing very little and warm sea all year. Mauritius has more to explore on land; the Maldives is about the water.

[Luang Prabang](/destinations/luang-prabang) in Laos is one of the most peaceful towns in Southeast Asia, with temples, the Mekong and waterfalls. Days start with the monks' alms giving at dawn and end at the night market.

The [Bacalar](/destinations/bacalar) lagoon in Mexico is a calm, freshwater alternative to the busy Caribbean coast, famous for its shades of blue. There are small hotels with docks over the water, and no waves at all.

sections.heading: How to keep it peaceful
sections.text:
- **Avoid the school holidays** if you can. Late May, June and September are quieter almost everywhere in Europe.
- **Pick a small hotel** or a villa, rather than a big resort.
- **Stay just outside the main town.** A short taxi or drive away is usually much calmer.
- **Plan less.** One or two outings a week is plenty on a relaxing holiday.
- **Go further for winter sun.** In Europe, Madeira and the Canary Islands are the warmest places in winter, and the quiet hotels fill up fast.

sections.heading: Can't agree how relaxing to make it?
sections.text: If one of you wants to do nothing and the other wants to see everything, our post on [planning a holiday when everyone wants something different](/blog/when-everyone-wants-a-different-holiday) has some ideas. Or put both kinds of trip on your list in somewhere🎉 and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Where is quiet for a holiday in Europe?
faqs.answer: Gozo, Menorca, Madeira and the Azores are among the quietest, especially outside July and August. Lake Garda and Sicily are calm in spring and autumn.

faqs.question: Where is good for a quiet holiday for couples?
faqs.answer: Gozo and Madeira are easy and peaceful, Matera is romantic for a few nights, and Mauritius and the Maldives are the classic far-away choices.

faqs.question: When is the quietest time to go on holiday?
faqs.answer: Late May, June and September are quieter than the summer holidays in most of Europe, and prices are lower too. January and February are quiet but colder, except in Madeira and the Canaries.
